title: Equalizers in the total category of an algebraic stack
statement: Fix the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal Z$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], viewed as its total category fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For every pair of parallel arrows $a,b:z\to z'$ in this total category, including arrows with different underlying scheme maps, there is an arrow $e:w\to z$ such that $ae=be$ and every arrow $t\to z$ equalizing $a,b$ factors uniquely through $e$. Thus the total category $\mathcal Z$ has equalizers. No separatedness or finiteness hypothesis on the diagonal is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06WY, lemma-fibre-products, (2) and (3): representable Isom presheaves imply equalizers; in particular algebraic stacks have equalizers.

proof.text: Write $U=p(z)$, $V=p(z\prime)$, $f=p(a)$ and $g=p(b)$. Construct the scheme equalizer using [def-pc-fibre-product]: put $P=V\times_S V$ and $W=U\times_{(f,g),P,\Delta_V}V$. Let $j:W\to U$ be the first projection. The pullback equation gives $fj=gj$. If $r:T\to U$ satisfies $fr=gr$, the pair $(r,fr)$ gives a unique map $T\to W$ above $r$; the second component of any such map must equal $fr$. Thus $j$ is the equalizer of $f,g$ among $S$-schemes, with no separatedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 06WY, proof of (2), first reduction: equalizer of the underlying scheme maps; scheme construction from Tag 01JO.

proof.text: Choose a lift $c:x\to z$ of $j:W\to U$ using the lifting axiom of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Put $A=ac$, $B=bc$, so $p(A)=p(B)=fj$. If $h:t\to z$ satisfies $ah=bh$, its base map factors uniquely as $p(h)=jr$ by step 1. The unique-factorization axiom of the same definition gives a unique $d:t\to x$ over $r$ with $cd=h$, and then $Ad=Bd$. Conversely $Ad=Bd$ implies $a(cd)=b(cd)$. Therefore composing with $c$ identifies equalizing arrows for $A,B$ with equalizing arrows for the original $a,b$, preserving uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 06WY, proof of (2), restriction to W and reduction to equal underlying maps.

proof.text: The unique-factorization axiom of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], applied to $A,B$ over the same base map, gives $i:x\to x$ over $1_W$ with $Ai=B$. Applying it in reverse gives $k$ with $Bk=A$. Uniqueness applied to $Aik=A$ and $Bki=B$ gives $ik=ki=1_x$, so $i$ is an automorphism in the fibre over $W$. For every $d:t\to x$, the equality $Ad=Bd$ is $Ad=Aid$. Both $d$ and $id$ lie over the same map to $W$, so the same unique-factorization axiom applied to $A$ implies $d=id$. The converse follows by composition. This reduces the problem to identity versus $i$.

source.place: Tag 06WY, proof of (2), unique automorphism i with a i=b.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-isom-space-locally-finite-type] with $\mathcal X=\mathcal Z$, $T=W$ and both objects equal to $x$. It gives an algebraic space $q:G=\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal Z,W}(x)\to W$ representing the presheaf $T\mapsto\operatorname{Aut}(x|_T)$. We use only its representability conclusion. Under this natural representation, $1_x$ and $i$ give sections $e,\sigma:W\to G$. For a map $r:T\to W$, $er$ and $\sigma r$ represent $1_{x|_T}$ and $i|_T$ respectively. All hypotheses hold because $x$ is an object of the given algebraic stack over the scheme $W$. No separatedness or finite-diagonal hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: Tag 06WY, proof of (3): representable Isom presheaves, proved there using bootstrap.tex Tag 04TB (lemma-quotient-stack-isom) and algebraic.tex Tag 04T5 (lemma-stack-presentation). Existing stronger node: stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 04XR.

proof.text: By step 4, $G$ is an algebraic space over $W$, so by [def-trf-algebraic-space] its diagonal $G\to G\times_WG$ (product of sheaves on $W$-schemes) is representable: its pullback along any map $h_D\to G\times_WG$ from a $W$-scheme $D$ is represented by a scheme. Take $D=W$ and the map $(e,\sigma):h_W\to G\times_WG$; the pullback is a scheme $M$ with structure map $m:M\to W$. For a $W$-scheme $r:T\to W$ the $T$-points of this pullback are the $g\in G(T)$ with $(g,g)=(er,\sigma r)$, a single point if $er=\sigma r$ and none otherwise. Thus $M$ represents $W\times_{e,G,\sigma}W$: a $T$-point of the latter is a pair $r_1,r_2:T\to W$ with $er_1=\sigma r_2$, and applying $q$ (with $qe=q\sigma=1_W$) gives $r_1=r_2$. Since $er$ and $\sigma r$ represent $1_{x|_T}$ and $i|_T$ (step 4), $l\mapsto ml$ is a bijection from maps $T\to M$ to maps $r:T\to W$ with $i|_T=1_{x|_T}$; in particular $m$ is a monomorphism. This is the scheme-base case of Tag 03KP (lemma-section-immersion), proved directly from the representable diagonal, with no immersion or separatedness assertion.

source.place: Tag 06WY, proof of (2), M=U times_G U; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03KP (lemma-section-immersion), (1). Its needed special case is proved here from the representable diagonal.

proof.text: Choose a lift $v:x_M\to x$ of $m$. By step 5, $i|_M=1_{x_M}$, which means $iv=v$ under the cartesian pullback identification. Thus $Av=Bv$ by step 3, and $E=cv:x_M\to z$ satisfies $aE=bE$. For any $h:t\to z$ with $ah=bh$, step 2 supplies the unique $d:t\to x$ over $r:p(t)\to W$ with $cd=h$. Step 3 gives $id=d$. Factor $d$ through a chosen pullback lift $u:x|_{p(t)}\to x$ over $r$: its comparison $t\to x|_{p(t)}$ is an isomorphism, since both objects lie over $p(t)$ and the unique-factorization axiom gives its inverse. The identity $id=d$ therefore says $i|_{p(t)}=1$. Step 5 yields a unique $l:p(t)\to M$ with $ml=r$. The same axiom applied to $v$ gives a unique $k:t\to x_M$ over $l$ with $vk=d$, and $Ek=h$. For uniqueness, any $k\prime$ with $Ek\prime=h$ has $m p(k\prime)=r$: the base factor through $j$ is unique by step 1. Uniqueness of factorization through $c$ gives $vk\prime=d$, and uniqueness of $l$ then gives $p(k\prime)=l$; uniqueness through $v$ yields $k\prime=k$. Hence $E$ is the required equalizer in the total category.

source.place: Tag 06WY, proof of (2), final assertion that x restricted to M is the equalizer; explicit existence and uniqueness, then undoing both reductions.

proof_origin.place: Tag 06WY, lemma-fibre-products (2)/(3), complete scheme-equalizer, automorphism and equality-locus construction; final universal property expanded.
